title: The hinge ladder: five rungs to lifting her off the floor
caption: How to lift a toddler off the floor: five hinge rungs, in tier order, with the reps and the exact test for moving up. Glute Bridge, Standing Hip Hinge, Hinge and Reach, Single-Leg Hip Hinge, then Single-Leg Hip Thrust at the top. The laundry basket, the box and the toddler are the same lift. Save the ladder.

overlays.text: Ten hip hinges a day and the laundry basket stops being a thing.

scenes.footer: Ready when you can hold the top for two seconds.

overlays.text: Glute Bridge. 10 reps. Lie on your back, feet flat, push your hips up.

scenes.footer: Ready when your back stays flat for all 10.

overlays.text: Standing Hip Hinge. 10 reps. Push your hips back, keep your back flat, stand up.

scenes.footer: Ready when your hands reach your shins without rounding.

overlays.text: Hinge and Reach. 10 reps. Reach both hands down your shins, then stand tall.

scenes.footer: Ready when the back foot stays off the floor.

overlays.text: Single-Leg Hip Hinge. 6 each side. Hinge on one leg, back leg straight behind you.

scenes.footer: This is the strength behind the lift.

overlays.text: Single-Leg Hip Thrust. 6 each side. Shoulders on the chair, one foot down, drive up.
The top rung takes months, not a week.
